title: Forward and Inverse Kinematics of a Planar Arm

contract.reader: A student or engineer who has the previous entry's homogeneous transforms and wants to command a robot arm by where its gripper should be
contract.problem: Tasks are stated in gripper coordinates but arms are driven through joints; the reader needs both directions and to understand why the inverse has several, infinitely many or no answers and misbehaves near singular postures
contract.outcome: Compute forward kinematics and workspace of a two-link arm; solve inverse kinematics in closed form with atan2 and choose between solutions; derive the Jacobian and its singularities; run Newton and damped-least-squares iterations and know when each fails; explain redundancy and what carries over to six-joint arms
contract.contribution: One example arm carried through every section, including both IK postures, Newton convergence and a side-by-side Newton versus damped step for an unreachable target
contract.evidence: Derivations and worked numbers; a figure of the two postures and workspace; three exercises; Craig (2005), Denavit and Hartenberg (1955), Lynch and Park (2017), Pieper (1968), Siciliano et al. (2009)
contract.limitations: Planar two-link arm only; Denavit-Hartenberg and product of exponentials named, not developed; no dynamics; no code

findings.problem: At 360 px the workspace radius loses its cos theta2 term, the shoulder-angle formula loses its second atan2 argument, the Newton step hides Delta q and q_{k+1}, and the worked example hides y and phi
findings.whyItMatters: These are results the text relies on immediately (the radius depends only on the elbow angle; the shoulder angle completes the closed-form IK; the Newton update is the method of Section 6)
findings.action: Break the displays over lines: two forms of r on two lines; theta1 with the second atan2 on its own line or via a named angle; Newton equations one per line; example x, y, phi in an aligned block
findings.acceptance: On new captures at 360 px, light and dark, the four displays are fully visible without sideways scrolling

findings.problem: At 1280 px phi = 75 degrees is hidden at the right of the example display
findings.whyItMatters: Small; the example is carried through the entry
findings.action: Covered by the aligned block of L1
